title: This Bell Has Rung 10 Billion Times on the Same Batteries 🔔
description:
This bell in Oxford has been ringing almost nonstop since 1840, on the same batteries. About ten billion rings so far, and nobody knows exactly what's inside them.

Two little brass bells sit on top of two tall dry batteries. A metal ball smaller than a pea hangs between them: one bell charges it and pushes it away, the other pulls it in, twice every second. It kept going through two world wars, the first planes and the moon landing. You can't even hear it: it's sealed behind two layers of glass, and its batteries are coated in sulfur, so their recipe is still a mystery.

Would you open it to find out? Tell us below.
